promises.quote: The ICB has taken this matter seriously and the executive leadership of the ICB were presented with a paper in a formal executive group meeting. The paper provided an analysis of this issue and a proposal for how it should be addressed. The meeting took place on the 8 July 2024 and supported the proposal; which is described in this letter.
promises.summary: ICB will attend MASH meetings on behalf of GPs

promises.quote: We are continuing to work with colleagues through the Domestic Homicide Review process to identify actions stemming from the Senior Coroner's proposed recommendations.
promises.summary: Continue working with Domestic Homicide Review to identify actions from recommendations

concerns.quote: During the course of these inquests, the evidence has revealed matters giving rise to concern.
concerns.hazard: inadequate discharge summary reflecting uncertainty in diagnosis

concerns.quote: A failure to advise Sally, as Nearest Relative, of her statutory right to request [REDACTED] assessment under the MHA
concerns.hazard: failure to inform Nearest Relative of statutory right to request assessment

concerns.quote: A delay of five months in putting into the RiO records a detailed timeline provided by Sally while [REDACTED] was an in-patient
concerns.hazard: delay in updating RiO records with patient timeline

concerns.quote: A failure to discuss with Sally or the maternal side of [REDACTED] family how he presented, notwithstanding a clear direction following a first ward round to 'collaborate' with the family
concerns.hazard: failure to discuss patient presentation with family despite collaboration directive

concerns.quote: A lack of understanding or professional curiosity about drug-taking and the extent to which, if at all, this contributed to [REDACTED] presentation
concerns.hazard: lack of professional curiosity about substance use impact

concerns.quote: whether Callum presented with an imminent and significant risk of harm to justify a short-term admission into hospital as is provided for in NICE guidance
Callum was asked whether he wanted his mother (who he described as his rock) notified of his discharge.
Nearest Relative details on the MH 1 form were not completed
obvious gaps' in the record keeping and that as Callum's mother was one of the few levers available to the assessing team, Callum's decision not to involve her should have been explored further
